sections.heading: Overshoot from slow voltage loop
sections.text: Forward converter overshoot: the voltage loop is too slow for the load step. Switch to peak-current-mode for faster response. If already on current-mode, reduce the voltage-loop kp and increase ki for faster recovery without overshoot.

sections.heading: Slow settling from reset-winding limitation
sections.text: If the forward converter settles slowly, check the transformer reset. D must stay below 0.5 for volt-second balance with a reset winding. If the duty cycle is near 0.5, the reset time is minimal and the transformer may not fully reset — this causes rising magnetizing current and eventual saturation.

sections.heading: Excess ripple from output inductor
sections.text: Output ripple is set by the output inductor current ripple and capacitor ESR. The forward converter has the same output stage as a buck. Recheck L, C, and ESR before changing gains.

sections.heading: Subharmonic oscillation
sections.text: Period-doubling near fsw/2 is subharmonic instability from peak-current-mode without slope compensation. Add ramp >= V_out/(N*L_out*fsw). This is an architecture fix, not a tuning fix.

sections.heading: Architecture limit
sections.text: If the forward converter cannot meet specs, consider: (1) two-switch forward for higher power and better reset, (2) push-pull or half-bridge for higher power, (3) flyback for simpler isolated design at lower power.
